issues.claim: 46 feet 4 of extension at the basement and 27 feet 9 at the first and second floors
issues.problem: Neither dimension is an extension depth. On A-300 (and A-400, A-500) the 46'-4 1/4" [46.35] line runs from the EXISTING/PROPOSED line (the existing upper-floor rear wall) to the rear lot line, and the 27'-9" [27.75] line runs from the outer edge of the new second-floor balcony to the lot line. The basement extension itself is only about 23'-9" deep plus a 1'-0" wall (A-101 dimension string: 1'-8" / 23'-9" / 1'-0" / 21'-9 1/4" rear yard), and the first/second-floor extension is about 15'-5" deep (Z-100 second-floor area B = 15.40 x 29.96 = 461.23 SF). Pricing a 46-foot-deep two-level extension roughly doubles the real scope.
issues.correction: Say: the section dimensions 46'-4 1/4" and 27'-9" are measured to the rear lot line (from the existing rear wall and from the new balcony edge). The new basement extension is about 23'-9" deep leaving a 21'-9 1/4" rear yard; the first/second-floor extension is about 15'-5" deep (461 SF zoning floor area) leaving a 30'-11 1/2" residential rear yard.
issues.evidence: A-300 and A-400: 46'-4 1/4" dimension starts at the EXISTING | PROPOSED arrow and ends at LOT LINE; 27'-9" starts at the balcony rail. A-101 top dimension string 23'-9" / 1'-0" / 21'-9 1/4"; Z-100 yard table: commercial rear yard 21'-9 1/4", residential rear yard 30'-11 1/2"; Z-100 second floor B = 15.40 x 29.96 = 461.23 SF. Arithmetic: 23.75 + 1.0 + 21.77 = 46.5 ~ 46.35; 46.35 - 15.40 = 30.95 = 30'-11 1/2".

issues.claim: under 1 foot thick, 4 foot tall foundation walls ... The concrete volume table totals 117 linear feet of new wall and 47.66 cubic yards
issues.problem: The table's wall line reads 'WALL 1' THICK X 4' TALL = 1 X 9 X 117.02 = 1052.85 CU FT'. The 47.66 CY total is computed with a 9-foot wall height, not 4 feet. If the wall is really 4' tall the volume is about 702 CF = 26 CY; if it is 9' tall (full cellar depth, which the sections suggest) the label is wrong. Either way the two numbers the script quotes cannot both be true, and the concrete and formwork price depends on which one is.
issues.correction: Say the table labels the wall '1' thick x 4' tall' but computes it at 9' tall (1 x 9 x 117.02 = 1,052.85 CF); the 47.66 CY total assumes a 9-foot wall. Confirm the wall height with the architect before pricing concrete.
issues.evidence: A-100 CONCRETE VOLUME CALCULATIONS: '2. WALL 1' THICK X 4' TALL = 1 X 9 X 117.02 = 1052.85 CU FT'; 'TOTAL = 1286.81 CU FT'; '47.66 CU YD = 1286.89 CU FT'. 1286.81 / 27 = 47.66.

issues.kind: misstated code threshold / sheet conflict not flagged
issues.claim: The occupant load is capped at 75 people, 70 regular seats and 4 ADA positions, which keeps it at the threshold for a place of assembly certificate
issues.problem: The sheet is internally inconsistent and the script papers over it. Note 2 says a place of assembly certificate is required at 75 or more people and claims 'PROPOSED 74 PEOPLE THEREFOR CERTIFICATE OF OPERATION NOT REQUIRED'; the seat count is 70 + 4 = 74; but the occupant load table and the posted sign say 75, and the capacity sign block says 'MAX. FLOOR OCCUPANCY = 113 PERSONS'. Whether a PA certificate is required is a cost and schedule decision.
issues.correction: Say: seats total 74 (70 regular + 4 ADA). Note 2 relies on 74 people to avoid a place of assembly certificate (required at 75 or more), but the occupant load table and the sign say 75 and the capacity sign block says 113. Get the number resolved before bid.
issues.evidence: A-101 NOTE 2: 'PLACE OF ASSEMBLY CERTIFICATE IS REQUIRED WHEN 75 OR MORE PEOPLE GATHER INDOORS. FLOOR OCCUPANCY = 113 PERSONS'.

coverage: A-400 (Section B-B, page 16) is never cited. It shows the same extension in section and a new poured-concrete cellar egress stair at the front of the building.

A-100 shows new poured concrete work at the FRONT as well as the rear: a new stair enclosure and a window well with ladder, both tied to the existing with #5 epoxied dowels, plus direct vents and a 144 sq in fresh air intake for the mechanical room. The 117.02 LF of new wall includes these.
Footing size conflict: EN-100 foundation wall detail calls out a 2'-6" x 1'-0" footing with 3 #5 bars and #4 vertical bars at 64" o.c.; A-100 and the concrete table use a 2'-0" x 1'-0" footing.

New exterior wall conflict: T-100 legend type 4 is 5 1/2" steel studs with 3 layers of 5/8" board and EN-100 lists 'new steel frame walls' at R-13 cavity + R-10 continuous, but A-300/A-500 specify 2x6 wood studs at 16" o.c. with R-19 and 3 layers of 1/2" board. The energy compliance path does not match the wall drawn. Type 1 partition is 2x6 on T-100 but 2x4 on the EN-100 detail.

Demolition note 24 says the demolition scope includes 'ALL WOOD JOISTS AND FRAMING, ALL MASONRY WHERE SHOWN'; note 20 puts all disposal fees on the contractor; note 30 tells the contractor to coordinate with HVAC, plumbing, electrical and structural drawings, which implies other drawings exist that are not in this set.

A new laundry room (104.27 SF) with washer/dryer and 2 compartment sink is built at the cellar (A-100), and two sump pumps are shown. The existing cellar also keeps a walk-in freezer, grease trap, 3 compartment sink and 2 compartment sink that remain in service.
New skylights: A-101 shows a 'NEW SKYLIGHT' strip beside Area C and 'SKYLIGHTS' over Area E (U-factor 0.60), in addition to the existing skylight that is retained.

First-floor capacity sign reads '55 PERSONS WITH MOVABLE SEATS OR 206 PERSONS STANDING'; the 'dangerous and unlawful' sign text on both A-101 and A-102 says 113 persons. These conflicts affect the PA filing.

Plumbing note 25 requires dry wells at locations on an SD 1-2 application filed with DEP; note 11 requires a watertight frost-proof water meter pit; the gas riser shows three gas meters (basement & 1st, 2nd, 3rd) and 3/4" branches off 1" risers.

Z-100 lists the building as Construction Class 3 non-fireproof under the old (1968) code, and the egress tables on A-101/A-102 are all 1968 BC references; that governs which fire-rating assemblies apply.
The pond, stone pavers and existing tree are shown retained on all proposed plans immediately beside the extension; new 'UP 2' steps lead from Area E to the yard.
